messages:
maya: saw a spike of preemptible evictions in us-west1 around 08:10 UTC, ~1.8% of runtime pods. some streams cut mid-request. need a practical, low-risk cutover pattern for streaming token handoff + KV cache reuse.

sahil: can you paste the alert logs?

maya: evict-bot: alert: preemptible_reclaims=324 window=10m region=us-west1

liam: 1. prefer seamless token stream cutover: start new stream on standby pod and stitch KV prefixes for resumed sessions. 2. fallback: requeue request to cpu path if no standby available.

zoe: +1 but stitching KV is tricky w/ different quantized variants. we should avoid cross-variant replay unless checksum matches.

maya: agreed. proposal:
- detect impending reclaim (GCP lifecycle notify) -> mark session as 'stitchable' if kv_shard checksum == standby_shard checksum
- prefetch last-kv-range to standby asynchronously (non-blocking)
- start tokens on standby with prefix replay of last 64 tokens, then continue from client stream
- if checksum mismatch or prefetch fails -> enqueue request to durable queue (kafka) and return 503 to client with retry-after header

sahil: sample pseudocode for detection: ```
if (lifecycleEvent == PREEMPTION && remaining_grace > 10s) {
  markSession(sessionId, STITCHABLE)
  sendPrefetch(sessionId, standbyNode)
}
```

liam: + add metric events: stitch_attempt, stitch_success, stitch_fallback_requeue. keep SLO target: <=75ms extra latency for stitch path, <=2s p99 for requeue.

zoe: also add a safety TTL on prefetched KV (30s) and a max memory cap per-standby to avoid huge prefetch storms. include rate limiter QPS per standby.

maya: ops-bot: can we run a canary across 10% of ephemeral pool for 6 hours with above flow?

ops-bot: scheduled: canary "stream-stitch-canary" -> us-west1, 10% pool, start 2024-06-13T09:00Z, duration 6h.

sahil: test plan:
- synthetic load generating graceful and abrupt drains (kill -9 vs preempt event)
- assert no data corruption (checksum)
- measure latency delta between normal, stitch, and requeue
- validate billing: prefetch bandwidth and standby memory impact

liam: rollout strategy: feature flag at route level: off -> requeue-only, canary -> stitch-enabled for 10% customers, ramp to 50% if errors <0.1% and stitch_success>99.5%. emergency kill-switch toggles to force requeue.

maya: 👌ui for SRE: add Grafana panel with metrics: preempt_events, stitch_attempt, stitch_success_rate, requeue_rate, stitch_latency_p50/p95/p99, standby_mem_pressure.

zoe: question on model variants: when standby uses a quantized variant we must short-circuit to requeue unless kv checksum matches same-arch marker. add marker to model metadata.

maya: agreed. also add retention: ephemeral prefetch artifacts deleted after session end or TTL.

sahil: will add small experiment: allow partial-kv-stitch where only the last N layers of KV are prefetched and a partial replay is performed; fallback easier. but start conservative (full-prefix up to 64 tokens).

liam: doc tasks: eng-runtime to write short playbook with sequence diagram and rollback steps. I'd like runbook entries for oncall: how to flip to requeue-only, how to inspect a failed stitch (logs + checksums).

maya: volunteers: liam -> playbook, zoe -> prefetch safety limits, sahil -> canary infra and feature flag. i'll own metrics/dashboard and runbook.

zoe: timeline?

maya: aim for canary next week Tue -> 2024-06-18. liam/zoe/sahil can we sync Mon 09:30PT to finalize configs?

liam: i can.

sahil: yes.

zoe: yes.

evict-bot: info: last_preempt_event_us-west1=2024-06-11T08:10:12Z, active_preempt_count=2

maya: thanks. will post a short RFC in #eng-infra once we have the playbook draft.

liam: one more thought — add a cheap checksum bloom filter per-shard to reduce prefetch traffic. cheap to compute and conservative.

zoe: love it.

maya: ok closing thread for now. meet Monday. :thumbsup:
